forefront: The officers are elected and have been replaced by vote.
healthy: Some of that standard is already on the record.
history: Adventism was born from a specific, dated, public failure.
branches: Seventh-day Adventism is one unified worldwide organization under the General Conference.
money: Tithe here is unusually structured and unusually opaque at the point where it matters.
reach: Members were not told what their leaders had said among themselves.
techniques: Thirty named techniques from domestic-abuse and social-psychology research, applied to institutions, in the eight stages of the cycle.
loops: The seven loops below show how the practices connect, so that each step makes the next one easier and the last step feeds the first.
say-do: On finance and governance, expect a real process with a published outcome — this structure does that.
cost: The cost is social, familial, and professional rather than mandated.
ledger: The conference and union administrative structures benefit, and their authority over pastors runs through payroll.
who-gets-hurt: They fall hardest where a person has the least power inside the institution and the fewest places to go outside it.
tiers: Most of the institution's work is done below the General Conference, by people who see decisions without making them.
precedent: Restoration of a critic's standing where the institution's own research later confirmed his claim would revise the discard section.
voices: They were two women at the church's publishing house, Pacific Press, who took equal pay to federal court and won.
questions: What is the total compensation of the senior executives in our health system, and where can a member read it?
